input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility fixes for the four audited Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard-accessibility defects that the accessibility
audit enumerated in the four core Dashboard flows — project creation, workbench
spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. On completion, each flow
is fully operable with keyboard alone: focus is managed correctly in modals,
every control is reachable and operable, and visible focus indicators are
consistent across the audited flows.

## Scope

- Fix the focus-loss defects in modals identified by the audit across the four
  audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline
  run submission).
- Make every control in the audited flows reachable and operable by keyboard,
  eliminating the unreachable controls cited in the audit.
- Make visible focus indicators consistent across the audited flows.
- Address or explicitly disposition every defect enumerated in the audit report
  for the four flows.
- Verify via keyboard-only walkthrough of each of the four flows that it can be
  completed end to end.
- Out of scope: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require,
  and flows outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed end to end using
  keyboard only, verified by a keyboard-only walkthrough of each flow.
- No focus traps remain in the audited flows, and focus is no longer lost in
  the modals cited by the audit.
- No control in the audited flows is unreachable or inoperable by keyboard.
- Visible focus indicators are consistent across all controls in the audited
  flows.
- Every defect enumerated in the audit report for the four flows is fixed or
  has an explicit, recorded disposition.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)**: The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard,
  with no focus traps or unreachable controls.
- **HLR-2 (P1)**: Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited
  flows. Bundled with HLR-1: both are remediated over the same UI surfaces by
  the same team from the same audit defect enumeration; splitting would force a
  second pass over the same components.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation —
the VPAT and the product docs accessibility statement — to reflect the fixed
keyboard-accessibility state of the four audited Dashboard flows. It depends on
the Dashboard keyboard-accessibility fixes being implemented, since the
conformance claims describe that fixed state. Two public-sector customers
require the updated, published conformance statement before renewal.

## Scope

- Revise the VPAT conformance claims for the four audited flows (project
  creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) to
  reflect the implemented keyboard operability and focus-indicator fixes.
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to reflect the fixed
  state.
- Republish both through the Red Hat docs content process.
- Content outline:
  - VPAT: updated conformance claims for keyboard operability and focus
    visibility for the four audited flows, scoped to what the fixes deliver
    (no claims beyond the audited flows, and no screen-reader claims beyond
    what the keyboard fixes require).
  - Accessibility statement: current statement revised to describe the fixed
    keyboard-accessibility state and republished.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT is updated to reflect the fixed keyboard-operability and
  focus-indicator state of the four audited flows, and makes no conformance
  claims beyond the delivered fixes.
- The product docs accessibility statement is updated and republished.
- The updated documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented
  fixes by the engineering team that delivered them, and review findings are
  resolved.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)**: The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product
  docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed
  state, with technical review.
